content.content:
1→# CLAUDE.md
     2→
     3→This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
     4→
     5→## Project Status
     6→
     7→This is an **active contest submission** for the **IEEE GRSS 2026 Data Fusion Contest** (deadline: April 06, 2026). The `src/` modules contain working skeleton implementations that must be significantly extended. See `plan.md` for the full contest-aligned development plan.
     8→
     9→**Critical shift from original design**: The dataset is Capella Space X-band SAR (NOT Sentinel-1), accessed via public AWS S3 (`s3://capella-open-data/data/`, region `us-west-2`). The ML approach is **self-supervised** (Noise2Noise + physics-consistency losses) — there are no ground-truth clean interferograms. The model output is a **denoised complex interferogram + per-pixel uncertainty**, not a DEM directly.
    10→
    11→## Environment Setup
    12→
    13→```bash
    14→conda create -n insar-dem python=3.10
    15→conda activate insar-dem
    16→pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
    17→pip install -r requirements.txt
    18→pip install -e .  # editable install to use `src` as a package
    19→# Contest-specific additional packages
    20→pip install boto3 pystac capella-reader dask geopandas
    21→conda install -c conda-forge isce3  # for coregistration and orbit geometry
    22→```
    23→
    24→Verify setup:
    25→```python
    26→import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())
    27→import rasterio
    28→import pystac, boto3  # contest data access
    29→```
    30→
    31→Validate S3 data access (no authentication required):
    32→```bash
    33→aws s3 ls --no-sign-request s3://capella-open-data/data/
    34→```
    35→
    36→## Running Experiments
    37→
    38→**Baseline InSAR DEM (phase-to-height conversion):**
    39→```bash
    40→python experiments/baseline/run_baseline.py --config configs/experiment/baseline_sentinel1.yaml
    41→```
    42→
    43→**U-Net training:**
    44→```bash
    45→python experiments/enhanced/train_unet.py \
    46→    --data_config configs/data/sentinel1_example.yaml \
    47→    --model_config configs/model/unet_baseline.yaml \
    48→    --train_config configs/train/default.yaml
    49→```
    50→
    51→No test suite exists yet. Model checkpoint saves to `experiments/enhanced/checkpoints/unet_baseline_final.pt`.
    52→
    53→## Architecture
    54→
    55→### Data Flow
    56→
    57→```
    58→data/raw/          (SAR SLC acquisitions - not in git)
    59→    |
    60→    v (external: SNAP / ISCE2 / GAMMA)
    61→data/processed/    (interferograms, coherence maps, unwrapped phase .tif)
    62→    |
    63→    v (src/insar_processing/)
    64→data/reference/    (high-res reference DEMs for training targets)
    65→    |
    66→    v (dataset_preparation.py: sliding-window tiling)
    67→    tiles (interferogram + coherence -> target DEM patches)
    68→    |
    69→    v (experiments/enhanced/train_unet.py)
    70→    model checkpoint (.pt)
    71→```
    72→
    73→### Source Packages (`src/`)
    74→
    75→- **`insar_processing/io.py`** — `load_raster()`, `save_raster()`, `resample_raster()` using rasterio. All raster I/O goes through here.
    76→- **`insar_processing/baseline.py`** — `BaselineConfig` dataclass + `run_baseline()` which calls `phase_to_height()` (simplified geometry: `h = phase / (k * sin(theta))`). Note: the perpendicular baseline parameter is stored in config but not currently used in the height formula.
    77→- **`insar_processing/dataset_preparation.py`** — `TileConfig`, `sliding_window()` generator, `prepare_dem_tiles()` which requires all input rasters to be pre-aligned (same shape).
    78→- **`models/unet_baseline.py`** — `UNetBaseline`: encoder-decoder with skip connections. Input: `(B, 2, H, W)` (interferogram + coherence stacked). Output: `(B, 1, H, W)` (DEM).
    79→- **`evaluation/dem_metrics.py`** — `rmse()`, `mae()`, `bias()` with optional boolean mask.
    80→- **`visualization/plots.py`** — Plotting helpers for DEM comparison and error histograms.
    81→
    82→### Config Structure (`configs/`)
    83→
    84→YAML configs are loaded with `yaml.safe_load()` (no Hydra at runtime yet, though `hydra-core` is in requirements):
    85→- `configs/data/` — paths to interferogram, coherence, reference DEM; tile_size, stride
    86→- `configs/experiment/` — paths + sensor geometry (wavelength_m, incidence_angle_deg, perpendicular_baseline_m)
    87→- `configs/model/` — in_channels, out_channels, features list
    88→- `configs/train/` — learning_rate, num_epochs, output_dir
    89→
    90→### Key Design Decisions
    91→
    92→- All rasters must be **co-registered before tiling** — `prepare_dem_tiles()` asserts equal shapes.
    93→- The current training loop in `train_unet.py` processes tiles **one-by-one without DataLoader batching** (scaffold only; replace with proper `Dataset`/`DataLoader`).
    94→- Input tensor format: `(B, 2, H, W)` where channel 0 = interferogram, channel 1 = coherence.
    95→- Model outputs relative height (no absolute reference); absolute DEM requires an external reference elevation.
    96→
    97→### Contest-Required Components (not yet implemented)
    98→
    99→These are the critical missing pieces for the contest:
   100→
   101→| File | Purpose |
   102→|------|---------|
   103→| `src/insar_processing/pair_graph.py` | Pair-graph construction, edge Q_ij scoring |
   104→| `src/insar_processing/geometry.py` | B_perp from ISCE3 orbit geometry |
   105→| `src/insar_processing/filters.py` | Goldstein, NL-InSAR, BM3D baselines |
   106→| `src/insar_processing/sublook.py` | Sub-look splitting for Noise2Noise training |
   107→| `src/models/film_unet.py` | FiLM-conditioned U-Net (replaces `unet_baseline.py`) |
   108→| `src/losses/physics_losses.py` | N2N, closure-consistency, temporal, gradient losses |
   109→| `src/evaluation/closure_metrics.py` | All 5 contest metrics |
   110→| `scripts/download_subset.py` | STAC crawl → manifest → S3 download |
   111→| `scripts/preprocess_pairs.py` | Coregistration → interferogram → coherence |
   112→| `scripts/unwrap_snaphu.py` | SNAPHU unwrapping with coherence mask |
   113→| `eval/compute_metrics.py` | Contest metrics → tables + paper figures |
   114→| `REPRODUCIBILITY.md` | Contest-required: STAC URL, checksums, seeds |
   115→
   116→### Contest Success Metrics
   117→
   118→All implemented in `src/evaluation/closure_metrics.py`:
   119→
   120→1. **Triplet closure error** — `wrap(φ_ij + φ_jk − φ_ik)`, target: median ↓ ≥30%
   121→2. **Unwrap success rate** — ≥90% connected component coverage + closure gate, target: ↑ ≥15 pp
   122→3. **Percent usable pairs** — coherence > 0.35 + unwrap pass + closure gate, target: ↑ ≥25%
   123→4. **DEM NMAD** — `1.4826 × median(|e − median(e)|)`, target: ↓ ≥15%
   124→5. **Temporal consistency residual** — `‖W(Ax − φ̂)‖₂`, target: ↓ ≥20%
   125→
   126→### Key Design Decisions (Contest-Driven)
   127→
   128→- **Self-supervised training**: Noise2Noise via sub-look splits — no reference clean data needed
   129→- **Model output**: denoised complex interferogram (2ch) + log-variance uncertainty (1ch), NOT a DEM
   130→- **FiLM conditioning**: model is conditioned on `[Δt, Δθ_inc, Δθ_graze, B_perp, mode, look, SNR_proxy]`
   131→- **AOI-based train/val/test splits**: prevents geographic leakage (not tile-based random splits)
   132→- **Uncertainty integration**: predicted `σ²(p)` weights SNAPHU and SBAS inversion downstream
   133→

1→Learning-Assisted InSAR DEM Enhancement
     2→========================================
     3→
     4→Contest submission for the **[IEEE GRSS 2026 Data Fusion Contest](https://www.grss-ieee.org/community/technical-committees/2026-ieee-grss-data-fusion-contest/)**
     5→— *deadline: April 06, 2026.*
     6→
     7→This repository implements a **stack-aware, self-supervised deep learning pipeline** for improving Interferometric SAR (InSAR) products over large, geometry-diverse satellite stacks, with downstream improvements in DEM quality and time-series consistency.
     8→
     9→## Overview
    10→
    11→The contest provides a Capella Space X-band SAR dataset: ~1,582 unique collects enabling 17,000+ interferometric pairs across multiple AOIs, with substantial diversity in acquisition mode, incidence angle, look direction, and orbital geometry.
    12→
    13→A competitive entry must be **pair-graph-aware** and **geometry-conditioned**. Our approach:
    14→
    15→1. **Pair-graph construction** — build a graph (nodes = collects, edges = candidate pairs), score each edge by a quality formula `Q_ij` using temporal baseline, incidence difference, perpendicular baseline, and SNR proxies, then select a high-value subset for processing.
    16→2. **Baseline InSAR products** — coregistration (ISCE3 + capella-reader), interferogram formation, coherence estimation, classical filtering (Goldstein, NL-InSAR, BM3D), SNAPHU unwrapping.
    17→3. **Self-supervised DL enhancement** — a FiLM-conditioned U-Net trained without any ground-truth labels using Noise2Noise (sub-look splits) + closure-consistency + temporal-consistency + fringe-preservation losses. Outputs a denoised complex interferogram and per-pixel uncertainty map.
    18→4. **Uncertainty-weighted inversion** — predicted uncertainty weights SNAPHU and SBAS stack inversion to improve unwrapping and time-series products.
    19→5. **Evaluation** — five hard, physics-linked contest metrics computed against classical baselines.
    20→
    21→## Contest Metrics
    22→
    23→| Metric | Definition | Target |
    24→|--------|-----------|--------|
    25→| Triplet closure error | `median|wrap(φ_ij + φ_jk − φ_ik)|` on stable pixels | ↓ ≥30% |
    26→| Unwrap success rate | % interferograms with ≥90% connected coverage + closure gate | ↑ ≥15 pp |
    27→| Percent usable pairs | % edges passing coherence + unwrap + closure gates | ↑ ≥25% |
    28→| DEM NMAD | `1.4826 × median(|e − median(e)|)`, stable terrain | ↓ ≥15% |
    29→| Temporal consistency residual | SBAS inversion residual `‖W(Ax − φ̂)‖₂` | ↓ ≥20% |
    30→
    31→## Installation
    32→
    33→```bash
    34→conda create -n insar-dem python=3.10
    35→conda activate insar-dem
    36→
    37→# PyTorch with CUDA
    38→pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu121
    39→
    40→# Core dependencies
    41→pip install -r requirements.txt
    42→pip install -e .
    43→
    44→# Contest-specific packages
    45→pip install boto3 pystac capella-reader dask geopandas
    46→conda install -c conda-forge isce3
    47→```
    48→
    49→Verify:
    50→```bash
    51→python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
    52→aws s3 ls --no-sign-request s3://capella-open-data/data/
    53→```
    54→
    55→## Data Access
    56→
    57→Data is on a **public AWS S3 bucket** — no authentication required.
    58→
    59→- **S3 bucket**: `s3://capella-open-data/data/` (region: `us-west-2`)
    60→- **STAC catalog**: `https://capella-open-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/stac/catalog.json`
    61→- **Contest collection**: child link `"IEEE Data Contest 2026"` → `capella-open-data-ieee-data-contest/collection.json`
    62→
    63→The catalog is a **static STAC** (JSON files, no `/search` endpoint) — use `pystac` directly.
    64→
    65→```bash
    66→# Crawl catalog, select AOIs, build local manifest, download subset
    67→python scripts/download_subset.py \
    68→    --stac_root https://capella-open-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/stac/catalog.json \
    69→    --out_manifest data/manifests/subset_manifest.csv \
    70→    --out_dir data/raw/
    71→```
    72→
    73→Data format per collect: COG GeoTIFF (CInt16 complex SLC) + STAC JSON + extended JSON sidecar.
    74→
    75→## Workflows
    76→
    77→### 1. Baseline InSAR Pipeline
    78→
    79→```bash
    80→# Coregistration, interferogram formation, coherence, classical filtering, SNAPHU
    81→python scripts/preprocess_pairs.py \
    82→    --manifest data/manifests/subset_manifest.csv \
    83→    --out_dir data/processed/
    84→
    85→python scripts/unwrap_snaphu.py \
    86→    --processed_dir data/processed/ \
    87→    --coherence_threshold 0.35
    88→
    89→# Simplified phase-to-height DEM (existing scaffold)
    90→python experiments/baseline/run_baseline.py \
    91→    --config configs/experiment/baseline_sentinel1.yaml
    92→```
    93→
    94→### 2. Self-Supervised DL Training
    95→
    96→```bash
    97→python experiments/enhanced/train_film_unet.py \
    98→    --data_config configs/data/capella_aoi_selection.yaml \
    99→    --model_config configs/model/film_unet.yaml \
   100→    --train_config configs/train/contest.yaml
   101→```
   102→
   103→The model (`FiLMUNet`) takes a complex interferogram (2 channels: Re, Im) conditioned on acquisition geometry metadata, and outputs a denoised interferogram + per-pixel log-variance. Training is fully self-supervised via sub-look splits — no clean reference interferograms are required.
   104→
   105→### 3. Evaluation
   106→
   107→```bash
   108→python eval/compute_metrics.py \
   109→    --processed_dir data/processed/ \
   110→    --ref_dem data/reference/ \
   111→    --out_dir results/
   112→```
   113→
   114→Produces all five contest metrics per AOI and aggregated, plus figures for the paper.
   115→
   116→## Repository Structure
   117→
   118→```
   119→src/
   120→  insar_processing/
   121→    io.py                  # Rasterio-based raster I/O (load_raster, save_raster, resample_raster)
   122→    baseline.py            # BaselineConfig + phase-to-height conversion (run_baseline)
   123→    dataset_preparation.py # Sliding-window tiling (TileConfig, sliding_window, prepare_dem_tiles)
   124→    pair_graph.py          # [to build] pair-graph construction + Q_ij edge scoring
   125→    geometry.py            # [to build] B_perp from ISCE3 orbit geometry
   126→    filters.py             # [to build] Goldstein, NL-InSAR, BM3D baselines
   127→    sublook.py             # [to build] sub-look splits for Noise2Noise training
   128→  models/
   129→    unet_baseline.py       # Basic U-Net (in_channels=2 → out_channels=1)
   130→    film_unet.py           # [to build] FiLM-conditioned U-Net for contest submission
   131→  losses/
   132→    physics_losses.py      # [to build] N2N, closure, temporal, gradient losses
   133→  evaluation/
   134→    dem_metrics.py         # RMSE, MAE, bias
   135→    closure_metrics.py     # [to build] all 5 contest metrics
   136→  visualization/
   137→    plots.py               # DEM comparison + error histogram plots
   138→
   139→experiments/
   140→  baseline/run_baseline.py              # Phase-to-height DEM (existing scaffold)
   141→  enhanced/train_unet.py               # Basic U-Net training (existing scaffold)
   142→  enhanced/train_film_unet.py          # [to build] Contest DL training script
   143→
   144→scripts/                               # [to build] Download, preprocess, unwrap
   145→eval/                                  # [to build] Contest metrics + figures
   146→configs/
   147→  data/          # Data paths, AOI selection, tiling parameters
   148→  experiment/    # InSAR geometry parameters
   149→  model/         # Model architecture hyperparameters
   150→  train/         # Learning rate, epochs, checkpoint directory
   151→notebooks/       # Exploratory analysis and pair-graph visualization
   152→```
   153→
   154→## Development Plan
   155→
   156→See [`plan.md`](plan.md) for the week-by-week implementation schedule, detailed phase descriptions, metric definitions, DL loss formulas, ablation study design, and the reproducibility checklist required for contest submission.
   157→
   158→## Reproducibility
   159→
   160→See [`REPRODUCIBILITY.md`](REPRODUCIBILITY.md) (to be created) for the STAC root URL, contest collection ID, exact download manifest with checksums, fixed random seeds, and deterministic training settings — all required by the contest.
   161→

    24→## 1. Contest Overview and Objectives
    25→
    26→### 1.1 Context
    27→
    28→The IEEE GRSS 2026 Data Fusion Contest (DFC26) provides a **Capella Space commercial SAR stack**: ~1582 unique collects, enabling 17,000+ possible interferometric pairs across multiple AOIs, with substantial diversity in mode, incidence angle, look direction, and orbital geometry.
    29→
    30→Evaluation is **committee-based** (not leaderboard), rewarding:
    31→- Soundness and originality
    32→- Insight and effective dataset use
    33→- Scalability (optional but favorable)
    34→- Reproducibility (public code, one-command pipeline)
    35→
    36→**A winning approach must be explicitly stack-aware and geometry-aware.**
    37→
    38→### 1.2 Contest Objectives (maps to evaluation criteria)
    39→
    40→| ID | Objective |
    41→|----|-----------|
    42→| O1 | Increase stack usability under geometry diversity by improving interferogram quality and unwrapping reliability (closure + unwrap metrics) |
    43→| O2 | Improve downstream products: DEM (where geometry permits) and time-series consistency via uncertainty-weighted inversion |
    44→| O3 | Produce interpretable "temporal storytelling" artifacts: pair graphs, maps, timelines showing why the method helps |
    45→| O4 | Reproducibility: one-command pipeline from S3 download → results figures, plus trained weights and configs |
    46→
    47→### 1.3 Key Dates
    48→
    49→| Date | Event |
    50→|------|-------|
    51→| Feb 04, 2026 | Data released |
    52→| **Mar 05, 2026** | **Today — start of active development** |
    53→| **Apr 06, 2026** | **Submission deadline (23:59 AoE)** |
    54→| Apr 13, 2026 | Winners announced |
    55→| Apr 20, 2026 | Internal paper deadline |
    56→| Apr 28, 2026 | Final paper deadline |
    57→

    59→
    60→## 2. Dataset: Capella Space SAR Open Data
    61→
    62→### 2.1 Data Access
    63→
    64→```bash
    65→# Validate open access (no authentication required)
    66→aws s3 ls --no-sign-request s3://capella-open-data/data/
    67→
    68→# Inventory dataset size
    69→aws s3 ls --no-sign-request --recursive --summarize s3://capella-open-data/data/ > s3_inventory.txt
    70→```
    71→
    72→- **S3 bucket**: `s3://capella-open-data/data/` (region: `us-west-2`)
    73→- **STAC root**: `https://capella-open-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/stac/catalog.json`
    74→- **Contest collection**: child link `"IEEE Data Contest 2026"` → `capella-open-data-ieee-data-contest/collection.json`
    75→- The catalog is **static STAC** (JSON files linked via root/child/item), NOT a STAC API — use `pystac`, not `pystac-client` unless building a local index.
    76→
    77→### 2.2 Product Format (Capella SLC)
    78→
    79→- **Format**: Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (`.tif`) + STAC JSON + extended JSON sidecar
    80→- **Pixel type**: Complex CInt16 (real Int16 + imaginary Int16 = 32 bits/pixel)
    81→- **Radiometric convention**: SLC relates to Beta Nought; a `scale_factor` in extended metadata converts to radar brightness
    82→- **Metadata parsing**: use `capella-reader` which provides orbit, Doppler, and ISCE3 adapter
    83→
    84→```python
    85→from capella_reader import CapellaSLC
    86→slc = CapellaSLC.from_file("path/to/slc.tif")
    87→orbit = slc.adapted.isce3_orbit  # ISCE3 orbit object
    88→```
    89→
    90→### 2.3 Compute/Storage Tiers
    91→
    92→| Tier | SLC count | Pair count | Storage | GPUs |
    93→|------|-----------|------------|---------|------|
    94→| Minimal (proof-of-pipeline) | 40–120 | 300–1500 | 1–3 TB | 1×24 GB |
    95→| Competitive (3–6 AOIs, multi-mode) | 200–600 | 3k–15k | 6–20 TB | 2×48 GB |
    96→| Ideal (many AOIs/modes) | 800–1582 | 10k–30k | 20–60 TB | 4–8×80 GB |
    97→
    98→**Target**: Competitive tier minimum to claim cross-geometry generalization.
